sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from the selected law \(p=P(E,W,Z\mid S=1)\), with an independent margin multinomial sample in design A when margins are estimated and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one draw of \((E,W,Z)\) conditional on \(S=1\); the finite SCM is a superpopulation model.
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) is binary and may be confounded with the response type; in design B its assignment probability may depend on \((U,Z)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All population selected-table cells are positive, so every \(v_e(z)\) used for normalization is positive and every compatible population cell margin is positive. Wald inference additionally requires an incident rigid chart with slack at least \(\varepsilon\), twice continuously differentiable continuation, separation from incompatible chart closures, and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\). Boundary and transition laws remain covered by confidence-fiber inversion without rank stability. First-order equivalence of that inversion to the frozen Wald ellipse additionally requires a locally saturated observable chart.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Reduced multinomial coordinates use empirical frequencies and the block-diagonal plug-in covariance. The deterministic chart rule reports a Wald ellipse only after a separated rigid chart and positive-definite sandwich are certified; otherwise it reports the full-square fallback. Transition inference uses exact multinomial replicate tails, a Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson preliminary region, and Berger--Boos calibration over the complete causal target fiber.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 identify PN and PS under positive observed tables, invertible proxy matrices, and unequal determinant-ratio conditions.
Formula (5) identifies a causal effect under a proxy rank condition without identifying the measurement mechanism.
Proposition 3.3 characterizes infinitesimal rigidity of an exact nonnegative factorization by its admissible-motion cone.
Theorems 5--9 give necessary support conditions and sufficient sequential recovery conditions for selected NMF factors.
Theorem 1 gives sufficient positive-scattering thresholds for minimality and uniqueness of nonnegative tensor decompositions.
Theorem 3.4 gives a regular root-n estimator for a linear proximal target without uniqueness of the bridge solution.

Theorem 1 identifies all four response-type probabilities in a randomized experiment under positive conditional tables, \(W\perp Z\mid U\), \(X\perp(U,Z,W)\), invertible cell matrices, and unequal determinant ratios; equations (8)--(11) give plug-in estimators.

Theorem 1 identifies all four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types under Figure 2(b)'s IV-plus-proxy recursive factorization, the five invertibility requirements in condition (i), the cross-treatment second-column separation in condition (ii), and the two exclusion restrictions in condition (iii).

Theorems 2--5 give sound closed-form bounds for a representative family of discrete probabilities of causation from standard experimental and observational distributions, while general-dimensional tightness remains open in the current version.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without strong identification.
E-variable inversion yields exact anytime-valid confidence sets for contingency-table parameters.
Theorem 4 identifies PN and PS under exogeneity and monotonicity, and equations (15)--(18) give sharp bounds otherwise.

body.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, the response-cycle compiler gives a boundary-complete necessary-and-sufficient test for rigidity of the causal pair \(\tau=(\mathrm{PN},\mathrm{PS})\). Its exhaustive local modes retain inactive endpoints and equal-endpoint split vectors, while the IV design adds zero or active residual states, forest scales, the active-cycle product, and relevance. A one-copy connected-component evaluator then returns a common exact target, an incompatibility report, or two legal same-observable full SCMs; strict-positive twins are required only on interior support charts. The atlas agrees with the published regular proxy formulas and terminates with fixed-alphabet exact bounds relative to effective coefficient-field oracles. Wald inference is valid on separated smooth rigid strata, exact confidence-fiber coverage remains valid at every rank and support transition, and first-order profile--Wald agreement is limited to locally saturated observable charts. The GEUVADIS application is specified as a known-selection IV audit, but numerical classification still requires its released cell table and binarization inputs.

project_justification.gap: Published selected-proxy and IV-plus-proxy formulas identify response-type targets under regular invertibility and separation, but do not decide causal-target constancy across simultaneous rank loss, inactive latent rows, coincident endpoints, forced coefficient zeros, or unknown population margins coupled by response-level shared-instrument equations.
project_justification.niche: The four binary response types form a labeled causal cycle. Factorization uniqueness is stronger than necessary: \(\tau_C\) can be constant while nuisance endpoints or equal-endpoint split vectors move. The relevant object is therefore the target image of the full nonnegative SCM fiber, stratified by observable rank, support, incidence, residual, and cycle data.
project_justification.fill: The exhaustive edge-state atlas proves equality between its finite structural union and each normalized cycle fiber. After connected components are computed, one-copy target projection decides within- and cross-component agreement over the ordered input field, and the cycle-to-SCM lift converts every disagreement into legal observationally equivalent causal models. Exact output bounds, separated-chart Wald inference, and transition-robust exact coverage complete the operational map; profile--Wald Hausdorff equivalence is asserted only where the observable chart is locally saturated.

body.related_work: Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026), Theorem 1 and Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33), supply the selected four-response-type model and regular PN/PS inversions; the atlas proof establishes agreement on compatible laws there and extends the decision domain to all nonnegative rank/support faces. Shingaki and Kuroki (2023) identify all four response-type probabilities in a randomized no-selection proxy experiment, and the established experimental reduction verifies the exact label-converted overlap plus a selected assignment-boundary law. Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii), identify binary potential-outcome types under regular IV-plus-proxy matrix conditions; the overlap theorem derives the same PN/PS transformation and separately exhibits a selected rigid law with singular \(A_x^{\mathrm K}\), a scope separation rather than a subsumption claim. NMF rigidity and partial-identifiability results concern factor recovery, whereas this theorem classifies a causal target on a labeled shared-endpoint cycle. Basu, Pollack, and Roy (2006) supply the classical exact sign, sampling, projection, and connected-component algorithms used only after the causal structural charts have been proved exhaustive.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact structural theorem is finite-alphabet and its real-algebraic component evaluator has a conservative doubly-exponential worst-case envelope; no claim of numerical efficiency is made. Arbitrary real inputs are handled relative to effective arithmetic and sign oracles for their ordered coefficient field, while integer-polynomial bit bounds require explicitly rational encodings. The compiler returns a field expression only when its arithmetic actually constructs one and otherwise retains a real-univariate/Thom encoding. Wald conclusions exclude repeated-root, incompatible-chart, and singular-covariance regimes. Exact confidence coverage remains valid there, but confidence fibers need not shrink at genuinely nonidentified laws. Because the frozen profile deviance is measured from the saturated empirical likelihood, first-order Hausdorff agreement with the frozen Wald ellipse is proved only on locally saturated observable charts; lower-dimensional rank charts retain an additional model-fit quadratic. The GEUVADIS numerical audit is not completed because the frozen inputs do not contain its exact selected cell table or binarization thresholds.
body.honest_scope: The contribution is the causal structural atlas, not generic two-copy quantifier elimination: rank-two segment orientations and the four exhaustive rank-one modes are glued through shared response endpoints, and design B is refined by the proved residual forest. Exact real-algebraic machinery first computes each one-copy chart's connected components and only then projects its target graph. Legal boundary countermodels may contain zero mechanisms; strict positivity is asserted only for witnesses sampled from interior support charts. Empty fibers are reported as incompatible. Agreement with Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki, Shingaki--Kuroki, and Kawakami is confined to their compatible overlap domains. Known selection fixes population margins by normalization. Exact confidence coverage is universal, whereas profile--Wald first-order equivalence requires local observable saturation in addition to separation and smoothness. The application conclusion remains conditional on the causal graph, proxy exclusion, instrument exogeneity and relevance, the imposed selection scheme, and the unavailable numerical GEUVADIS table.
body.interpretation: Rigidity means that every full SCM compatible with the causal graph, selected law, and supplied information has the same PN/PS pair; it is not defined by an inverse formula or by uniqueness of the latent proxy factorization. A rigid certificate is therefore an identifying map from observables to the singleton causal target image. A nonrigid certificate consists of two legal full SCMs that agree on all supplied observables and margins but disagree on the causal target. An empty fiber is model incompatibility and is reported separately rather than being labeled rigid or nonidentified.
